intro: Vermont runs its elections town by town, through each town or city clerk.

id_rule.text: Most Vermont voters do not need to show ID. First-time voters who registered by mail do need to show ID. Ask your town clerk if you are not sure.

elections.name: General election
elections.hours: Polls open between 5:00 am and 10:00 am, set by each town, and close at 7:00 pm
elections.what: Federal, state and local offices, plus any statewide or local measures. Your exact ballot depends on where you live.

dates.label: Early voting begins
dates.detail: Early voting starts 45 days before the election, or as soon as ballots are ready. Ask your town or city clerk how and where you can vote early.

dates.label: Ballots mailed to every active voter
dates.detail: Vermont mails a general election ballot to every qualified voter. The mailing starts by Sept. 21 and must be finished by Oct. 1. You do not need to ask for one.

src.label: Vermont Secretary of State - 2026 elections calendar

dates.label: Mail ballot deadline and request deadline
dates.detail: A mailed ballot must reach your town clerk before the office closes on Nov. 2, or you can bring it to your polling place on Election Day. You can ask for a ballot until 5 pm or the clerk's closing time on this day.

dates.label: Last day to register to vote
dates.detail: Vermont has same-day registration. You can register any day up to and including Election Day, at your town clerk's office or at the polls.

src.label: Vermont Secretary of State - voter registration FAQs

dates.label: Election Day
dates.detail: Polls close at 7 pm. If you still have your mail ballot, bring it to your polling place before 7 pm.
